page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system includes 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support spans AVX, AVX-512, AES, and SHA-NI extensions. It includes no bundled local storage and operates with a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU throughput, reaching 3111.48 in stress-ng single-core tests and strong performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. Memory tests show a cached read bandwidth of 2464.13 GB/sec and an uncached large-block read speed of 96.08 GB/sec. Extended instruction processing and encryption tests reflect solid vector computation abilities. The primary tradeoff of this instance is its reliance on attached remote block storage, as no local NVMe SSDs are included, alongside a lean memory allocation per vCPU.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high clock frequency and dedicated AMD EPYC core density deliver substantial processing throughput per compute node without requiring over-provisioned RAM overhead. This configuration is particularly suited for high-density compute tasks such as software compilation, batch text and image processing, web serving, and compute-heavy microservices. However, memory-intensive data analytics or large in-memory databases may require instances with higher RAM-to-vCPU ratios.
